mŏdernus , a, um, adj. from modo, just now; like hodiernus from hodie,
I.modern (post-class.); as subst.: mŏderna , ōrum, n., things or institutions of the present: “antiquorum diligentissimus imitator, modernorum nobilissimus institutor,” Cassiod. Var. 4, 51 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
